 Versus

With
WPCRL/1621/2025
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
None appears on behalf of the petitioners, 
as the matter is being taken up on mention.
2. Mr. Tumul K. Nainwal, learned AGA for the 
State.
3. Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Mr. Sandeep Kothari, 
learned counsel for respondent no.8.
4. Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned Senior 
Advocate, submits that in the present writ 
petition, an order has been passed by a 
Co-ordinate Bench on 24.03.2026, wherein 
Mr. D.K. Sharma, learned Senior Advocate 
appearing for the petitioners, on instructions, 
undertook that petitioners are ready to hand 
over the keys of the property which they barged 
into after getting protection order from this 
Court.
5. Learned Senior Advocate appearing for 
respondent no.8 submits that, in the writ 
petition, a categorical averment has been made 
by petitioners that they are not in possession of  the property and had sought relief of possession 
from this Court in the writ petition. However, 
only protection for persons was granted. He also 
submits that, despite the undertaking given in 
the month of March 2026, for the last seven 
months, the keys have not been handed over for 
one pretext and the other.
6. In view of the above, list on 29.10.2026, on 
which date, petitioners shall remain physically 
present along with the keys of the property so 
that the order dated 24.03.2026 can be 
complied with.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
27.10.2026 AK

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
UKHC010009252026
WPCRL No.119 of 2026
Indu Pradhan and another ………Petitioners
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others ……Respondents
 With
WPCRL No.1621 of 2025
Sanjay Pradhan ………Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others ……Respondents
 
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Tumul K. Nainwal, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Arvind Vashistha, learned Senior Advocate assisted 
by Mr. Ashutosh Joshi, learned counsel holding brief of 
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for respondent no.8.
4. The Court is pained to see that an undertaking given by 
the learned Senior Advocate of this Court has not been 
fulfilled. The undertaking given before the Co-ordinate Bench 
on 24.03.2026, is reproduced hereinbelow:-
“Mr. D.K. Sharma learned counsel on instructions 
undertakes that petitioners are ready to handover the 
possession of the part of the proper except house the 
possession of which was after order of protection.”
5. Despite lapse of more than seven months the said 
undertaking has not been complied with on one pretext and 
the other.
6. This Court vide order dated 27.10.2026 directed 
petitioners to remain present before this Court physically along 
with keys of the property so that order dated 24.03.2026 can 
be complied with.
7. Today both petitioners – Indu Pradhan and Pradeep  2
Pradhan – are present before this Court, who are duly 
identified by their Advocates.
8. Since Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the 
petitioners is out of town due to some personal difficulty, 
therefore, it is requested on behalf of learned counsel for the 
petitioners that instead of handing over the keys of the 
property to Mr. Arvind Vashistha, learned Senior Advocate, 
they are ready to give the keys before this Court.
9. The keys are just now being handed over to Bench 
Secretary of this Court and the same shall be passed on to 
Registrar General of this Court who shall ensure the safe 
custody of the keys in a sealed cover.
10. List this case on 04.11.2026.
11. Personal presence of the petitioners are hereby 
exempted.
 
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 29.10.2026
SK
